{"id": "7cf21930-5a43-4ad5-bc89-8f58627c1e1d", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"thinking": "I'm now examining the WebACL configuration, noting the default allow action and the AntiDDoS managed rule set with its challenge sensitivity settings at priority 0.

The remaining rules include a rate-based rule that only counts (300 requests per 300 seconds per IP) plus several managed rule groups (IP reputation, common rules, known bad inputs, SQLi) all with OverrideAction None. The origin points to the EKS UI load balancer with no signed URL requirements or geo restrictions, so I'm concluding the 403s most likely stem from WAF blocking rather than distribution-level config.

I want to pull WAF BlockedRequests metrics against baseline to identify which rule actually triggered, check CloudFront's 403 error rate, and look through CloudTrail for any WAF rule changes right before the incident window — the AntiDDoS rule set feels particularly relevant given the time-bounded nature of the outage.

The incident title also hints at an Athena permission gap, suggesting WAF logs route to S3 and get queried via Athena, but there may be a denial blocking that investigation path. I'm planning to spawn parallel subagents: one pulling CloudFront metrics (4xx/5xx error rates, request counts, total errors) and another gathering WAF-specific metrics.

I'll also need WAFV2 rule-level stats to pinpoint which rule is blocking traffic for the relevant WebACL, a CloudTrail subagent to review recent WAF and CloudFront configuration changes over a wider window, and a subagent to check WAF logging status and attempt querying logs despite the possible Athena permission issue. I might peek at the logging config myself first before deciding how to delegate that piece.

I'll compare against a baseline window of 16:00-17:30 the same day before launching the subagents.

I'm setting up four parallel subagents against account 012345678901_1 in us-east-1: one for CloudFront metrics, one for WAF per-rule block/count metrics, one for CloudTrail change history, and one for WAF logging configuration and log queries. Launching all four now.

# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### HTTP 403 responses on CloudFront distribution EEXAMPLE000001
**Description:** Between 17:30 and 18:30 UTC on 2026-10-06, customers and automated clients received HTTP 403 (Forbidden) responses from CloudFront distribution EEXAMPLE000001 (domain d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net). The 403s were time-bounded (recovered after the window).
**Time:** 2026-10-06T17:30:00Z - 2026-10-06T18:30:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: AWS WAF CommonRuleSet blocked the requests, producing the 403s
**Description:** WAF BlockedRequests metrics (WebACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4, per-rule) attribute ALL blocks during the incident to a single rule: AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet. Other rules had ZERO blocks in the window (KnownBadInputs, SQLi, AntiDDoS, IpReputation), and the rate-based rule was Count-only. The block counts match the CloudFront 4xx pattern exactly in two bursts: ~50-60 blocks/min from 17:32-17:52, a gap, then ~30 blocks/min from 18:05-18:25. CloudFront 5xx was flat 0%; request volume was flat (~2,300-2,700/min) with no traffic surge, ruling out a volumetric DDoS. The step-on/step-off shape points to a config/rule toggle rather than gradual degradation.
**Cascades to:** symptom-403

### Cause: No control-plane config change — managed-rule evaluation, not an API change
**Description:** CloudTrail management-event search across 2026-10-05 17:00 → 2026-10-06 19:00 UTC (us-east-1, account 012345678901_1) found NO UpdateWebACL, no rule/rule-group/IP-set/logging-config change, and no paired apply/revert around 18:30. The only mutative event was a single CloudFront UpdateDistribution at 16:11:15 UTC, ruled out: 79 min before onset, never reverted, WebACL association unchanged, no geo-restriction/viewer-policy/custom-error/origin changes, routine Terraform apply. Therefore the abrupt onset/recovery is NOT attributable to any CloudTrail-recorded change; it is consistent with AWS WAF CommonRuleSet managed-rule evaluation reacting to request content (managed-rule versions can auto-update without a customer API call). This cause explains WHY CommonRuleSet began blocking without any operator action.
**Cascades to:** symptom-403

#### Gaps
- **Request-level WAF log detail unobtainable — IAM access denied:** Request-level WAF log detail (BLOCK action by terminatingRuleId, top client IPs/countries/URIs/user-agents, exact per-record onset/recovery) could NOT be obtained. The ready-made Athena table default.waf_logs (Glue db default, workgroup primary, engine v3) exists and is correctly configured with partition projection over the WAF log prefix, but every content path is denied for the principal [redacted ARN] athena:StartQueryExecution denied, s3:GetObject denied, s3:ListBucket at root denied (prefix-scoped ListBucket IS allowed, so only object metadata is reachable). Object-size analysis of the gzipped log files showed flat log volume baseline vs incident (no volume spike), corroborating the 'no DDoS' finding but not resolving the CommonRuleSet sub-rule / per-caller breakdown. Missing permissions: s3:GetObject on [redacted ARN]; athena:StartQueryExecution / GetQueryExecution / GetQueryResults; glue:GetTable / GetPartitions on default.waf_logs; and s3 read/write (GetObject+PutObject) on the Athena query-results location.

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Restore WAF-log visibility by attaching a scoped read-only inline policy to the investigating role, then run an Athena query over the incident window to classify the blocked traffic. Only if that analysis confirms the blocks were false positives on legitimate traffic should the AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet (CRS) rules be tuned via targeted RuleActionOverride-to-Count (conditional, NOT applied now).

## Reasoning
The confirmed cause is AWS WAF WebACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4, where AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet (priority 3, OverrideAction None, no RuleActionOverride) blocked ~1–2.5% of requests as HTTP 403 in two bursts. The incident self-recovered, so there is no active outage. It is NOT yet known whether the blocked traffic was legitimate (false positives) or malicious (correctly blocked) — and that distinction decides whether any WAF change is desirable. The only reason it cannot be resolved is an access gap: role DevOpsAgentRole-AgentSpace-0fa8fc344f02 lacks s3:GetObject on the WAF log bucket plus Athena and Glue read. Granting those scoped read-only permissions is the lowest-risk, immediately actionable step; it changes no customer-facing behavior and unblocks the analysis. Any CRS change is gated behind that analysis.

## Execution Plan

### Step 1: Prepare

#### 1.1 Capture any existing inline policy of this name as the rollback…
**Type:** command
```
aws iam get-role-policy --role-name DevOpsAgentRole-AgentSpace-0fa8fc344f02 --policy-name waf-log-read-access --region us-east-1
```
**Purpose:** Capture any existing inline policy of this name as the rollback baseline before adding the new one.
**Advisory:** A NoSuchEntity error confirms no prior version exists — rollback is then to delete the policy entirely. If it returns a policy, save its PolicyDocument verbatim to restore the exact prior version.

#### 1.2 Record the current WebACL config and LockToken as the rollback baseline…
**Type:** command
```
aws wafv2 get-web-acl --name CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 --id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4 --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1
```
**Purpose:** Record the current WebACL config and LockToken as the rollback baseline for the conditional CRS tuning; confirm CRS at priority 3 has no RuleActionOverride set.
**Advisory:** The LockToken is required for any later update-web-acl call and changes after every modification; re-read it immediately before an update.

### Step 2: Pre Validate

#### 2.1 Confirm the role has no conflicting inline policy named…
**Type:** command
```
aws iam list-role-policies --role-name DevOpsAgentRole-AgentSpace-0fa8fc344f02 --region us-east-1
```
**Purpose:** Confirm the role has no conflicting inline policy named waf-log-read-access so apply creates rather than silently overwrites.
**Advisory:** The role currently has no inline policies and three attached managed policies; the new inline policy must not touch those managed policies.

### Step 3: Apply

#### 3.1 Grant the minimum read-only permissions to query WAF logs: read the WAF…
**Type:** command
```
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name DevOpsAgentRole-AgentSpace-0fa8fc344f02 --policy-name waf-log-read-access --region us-east-1 --policy-document '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Sid":"ReadWafLogObjects","Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:GetObject","s3:ListBucket","s3:GetBucketLocation"],"Resource":["[redacted ARN]","[redacted ARN]"]},{"Sid":"AthenaQuery","Effect":"Allow","Action":["athena:StartQueryExecution","athena:GetQueryExecution","athena:GetQueryResults","athena:StopQueryExecution","athena:GetWorkGroup"],"Resource":"[redacted ARN]"},{"Sid":"GlueCatalogRead","Effect":"Allow","Action":["glue:GetDatabase","glue:GetTable","glue:GetPartitions"],"Resource":["[redacted ARN]","[redacted ARN]","[redacted ARN]"]}]}'
```
**Purpose:** Grant the minimum read-only permissions to query WAF logs: read the WAF log bucket, run/read Athena queries in the primary workgroup, and read the Glue entry for default.waf_logs.
**Risks:** Grants read access to raw WAF log data (request headers, client IPs, URIs); scope is limited to the one WAF log bucket, the primary Athena workgroup, and the default.waf_logs table — no write or config-change permission.
**Advisory:** The primary workgroup uses Athena-managed query results (no customer OutputLocation), so no s3:PutObject on a results bucket is needed; athena:GetQueryResults returns the managed results. If a custom OutputLocation is used, add matching s3:PutObject/GetObject on that prefix., If LakeFormation is later enabled on default.waf_logs, additional LakeFormation grants would be needed; it is currently not registered with LakeFormation.

### Step 4: Post Validate

#### 4.1 Confirm waf-log-read-access now appears in the role's inline policy list
**Type:** command
```
aws iam list-role-policies --role-name DevOpsAgentRole-AgentSpace-0fa8fc344f02 --region us-east-1
```
**Purpose:** Confirm waf-log-read-access now appears in the role's inline policy list.

#### 4.2 Verify the policy document contains exactly the expected S3, Athena…
**Type:** command
```
aws iam get-role-policy --role-name DevOpsAgentRole-AgentSpace-0fa8fc344f02 --policy-name waf-log-read-access --region us-east-1
```
**Purpose:** Verify the policy document contains exactly the expected S3, Athena, and Glue read statements and nothing broader.

#### 4.3 Run a test Athena query over the incident window to prove visibility is…
**Type:** command
```
SELECT terminatingruleid, httprequest.clientip, httprequest.country, httprequest.httpmethod, httprequest.uri, httprequest.headers, httprequest.args FROM default.waf_logs WHERE action='BLOCK' AND log_time BETWEEN '2026/10/06/17/30' AND '2026/10/06/18/30' LIMIT 200
```
**Purpose:** Run a test Athena query over the incident window to prove visibility is restored and begin the false-positive-vs-correct-block analysis (via aws athena start-query-execution --work-group primary --query-execution-context Database=default, then get-query-results).
**Advisory:** Classification: concentrated IPs, scanner/absent user agents, SSRF/LFI/XSS payloads, and hits on EC2MetaDataSSRF/GenericLFI/CrossSiteScripting => malicious, correctly blocked => make NO CRS change. Distributed real-customer IPs, legitimate browsers/known partners, benign URIs tripping SizeRestrictions/NoUserAgent_HEADER/RestrictedExtensions => false positives => justify the conditional tuning., The two abrupt bursts suggest a bounded source; group by clientip and terminatingruleid to see whether blocks concentrate on a few sources (malicious) or spread across many (false positive).

### Step 5: Rollback

#### 5.1 Return the role to its original permission set once the analysis is…
**Type:** command
```
aws iam delete-role-policy --role-name DevOpsAgentRole-AgentSpace-0fa8fc344f02 --policy-name waf-log-read-access --region us-east-1
```
**Purpose:** Return the role to its original permission set once the analysis is complete or the access is no longer needed.
**Advisory:** If the prepare step captured a pre-existing policy document, restore that exact document with put-role-policy instead of deleting.

## Code Change Specification

### Requirements

#### 1. CONDITIONAL — only if the WAF-log analysis confirms the blocked requests were false positives on legitimate traffic: tune the specific CRS sub-rules that caused them, using the narrowest possible override.
**Description:** Do NOT make any CRS change until the Athena analysis identifies which specific CRS sub-rules (e.g. NoUserAgent_HEADER, SizeRestrictions, RestrictedExtensions, BadBots) fired on confirmed-legitimate requests. When confirmed, prefer the least-permissive remedy in order: (1) a scope-down statement so the rule group is not evaluated for the specific legitimate path/host/client, (2) a RuleActionOverride setting ONLY the offending sub-rule(s) to Count (all other CRS rules stay at Block), or (3) a narrowly scoped Allow rule at higher priority matching only verified-legitimate traffic. Implement in the Terraform/IaC that owns the WebACL (CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4; stack is Terraform-managed) via a rule_action_override on the managed_rule_group_statement block, not a console-only change. CRS is at priority 3 with override_action None and no rule_action_override; capture the LockToken immediately before any manual update-web-acl.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- No CRS change is made unless the WAF-log analysis explicitly confirms the blocked traffic was legitimate (false positives); if malicious, the WebACL is left unchanged and the finding documented.
- Only the specific sub-rules the logs show caused false positives are overridden to Count or scoped out — the rest of CommonRuleSet and all other rule groups (AntiDDoS, IpReputation, KnownBadInputs, SQLi) remain at Block. No blanket loosening of CRS.
- The change is expressed in the Terraform/IaC that owns the WebACL so it is not reverted by the next apply, with a comment linking it to the 2026-10-06 incident and the confirming log evidence.
- After applying, WAF BlockedRequests for the previously-false-positive sub-rules on legitimate traffic drops to zero while blocks on genuinely malicious requests continue, verified via CloudWatch WAF metrics and a follow-up Athena query over a post-change window.

Do NOT make any CRS change until the Athena analysis identifies which specific CRS sub-rules (e.g. NoUserAgent_HEADER, SizeRestrictions, RestrictedExtensions, BadBots) fired on confirmed-legitimate requests. When confirmed, prefer the least-permissive remedy in order: (1) a scope-down statement so the rule group is not evaluated for the specific legitimate path/host/client, (2) a RuleActionOverride setting ONLY the offending sub-rule(s) to Count (all other CRS rules stay at Block), or (3) a narrowly scoped Allow rule at higher priority matching only verified-legitimate traffic. CRS is at priority 3 with override_action None and no rule_action_override; capture the LockToken immediately before any manual update-web-acl.

Acceptance criteria:
- No CRS change is made unless the WAF-log analysis explicitly confirms the blocked traffic was legitimate (false positives); if malicious, the WebACL is left unchanged and the finding documented.

- The change is expressed in the Terraform/IaC that owns the WebACL so it is not reverted by the next apply, with a comment linking it to the 2026-10-06 incident and the confirming log evidence.
- After applying, WAF BlockedRequests for the previously-false-positive sub-rules on legitimate traffic drops to zero while blocks on genuinely malicious requests continue, verified via CloudWatch WAF metrics and a follow-up Athena query over a post-change window.","children":[]}]}]}]}}
